title: 6th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 37 members present, accepted the minutes of two earlier sittings and announced committee changes, including moving Vaikaradhoo member Hussain Ziyad onto the Economic Committee. Most of the part was question time with the Minister of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development, Dr. Ali Haider Ahmed. Members pressed him on why the two-yearly minimum wage review was overdue, on the study the minister said would finish in December 2025, and on delays in regulations under the Industrial Relations Act; the minister repeatedly said he would only answer questions tied to the day's topic. Two government bills were listed for first reading, and the part ends partway through the opening of debate on a resolution by Kanditheemu member Ameen Faisal about overtime pay for education and health workers. This part opens mid-speech: a member (name given in part 1) criticises how the government spends the payroll budget, arguing the money should go to education and health rather than political appointees, military-grade vehicles and parades. The chair then gave the floor to Dr. Anara Naeem, who welcomed the government's focus on education and health, citing hiring, scholarships, free degree programmes and construction of health centres, hospitals and schools. The chair allowed the debate on the resolution to continue later, read out the day's committee schedule, and adjourned; the next sitting is set for Tuesday 24 June 2025 at 9:00.

speakers.name: Dr. Ali Haider Ahmed
positions: As Minister of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development, said the minimum wage study should finish by December 2025 and technical help is being sought from the ILO.
Said many questions were outside the day's topic and declined to answer them, and that he could not give figures on study costs or unions.
Said regulations under the Industrial Relations Act had been sent to the Vice President's office and he gave technical capacity gaps as a cause of delay.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked why the legally required two-yearly minimum wage review has been overdue since January 2022 and said no study had been shared with the board.
Pressed the minister on the board's budget and pay, delays in Industrial Relations Act regulations and the independence of the Director General.
In the debate, welcomed the resolution and said safe working conditions for education and health workers are vital to the country's future.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked whether the minimum wage had brought positive changes and whether the study could slip past December 2025.
Asked what had been done to reach the 60 percent Maldivian senior management target and how many WhatsApp groups of students had been formed.
Raised complaints of barriers to women's employment, including six-month maternity leave, and asked which jobs are reserved for Maldivians.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked whether the minister knew Islamic University of Maldives students could not sit exams because the ministry had not paid their fees.
Asked how much had been spent on minimum wage studies and why the November 2023 review was not carried out.
In the debate, spoke on teachers' and health workers' overtime, citing MVR 569.8 million and criticising the previous government's spending choices.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked about the minister's power to set maximum working hours and what had been done on the 50 percent Maldivian HR head and 60 percent senior management rules.
Asked whether unions and collective bargaining agreements are useful for harmonious industries.
Moved the resolution seeking MPs' views on overtime pay for education and health workers and urged cross-party debate to find a solution.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked what policy addresses foreign workers being left out of the minimum wage, which he said displaces Maldivians from jobs.
Raised the difficulty families face sending money to children studying abroad and said the ministry does not reply.
Asked whether the ministry carries full responsibility for protecting workers and their unions' rights.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked whether the report on pay and allowance changes required by law had been prepared and by what date, repeating it when unanswered.
Asked about the Industrial Relations Division lacking budget and facilities, and how complaints to those bodies are handled.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked whether any study shows more Maldivians working in tourism since the minimum wage was set.
Asked how many countries have laws giving a minimum wage to only some groups of workers.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked whether any action had been taken against employers breaking the minimum wage law in two years.
Asked how often the minister met social partners and why the annual tripartite labour dialogue forum had not been held.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked whether the minimum wage law was passed without a study and whether other countries review wages.
Asked how many resorts arrange night ferries so staff can return to their islands.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked whether setting minimum wage and higher education opportunities fall within the minister's mandate, citing a pilot training dispute.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when students who applied for higher education loans would get an answer and when loans would be paid out.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked whether a minimum wage should exist, how fixed allowances are treated in setting it, and whether a completion date could be given.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked the minister to give details of the study and whether he accepts it is his own responsibility.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked whether the minister accepts the previous government should have set the minimum wage under the November 2023 review.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked how many unions and federations have registered under the Industrial Relations Act and whether any employers' union exists.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked what is being done to make workers aware of the Act and whether obstacles to enforcing it have been identified.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Welcomed the government's priority on education and health, citing hiring, scholarships, free degrees and building and repairing schools, health centres and hospitals.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2025/2/1 and 2025/2/2 were declared accepted as no amendments were proposed.
Hussain Ziyad (Vaikaradhoo) was appointed to the Economic Committee in place of Ibrahim Nazil.
Question time was closed after the minister's answers to questions 6.1 and 6.2.
Debate time on the overtime resolution was set at about four hours, shared out by party.
The chair ended the debate for the day so committees could meet as scheduled.
Committee meetings were announced for the Finance, ICT, Economic, National Development and Heritage, and Decentralisation committees.
The next sitting was set for Tuesday 24 June 2025 at 9:00.
